story: On a sunny Sunday evening at 7:17, Gary is bench-testing light strings and a speaker in his garage, sketching out wiring for Hal with a hopeful focus. Donna, cheerful as ever, is heading up Magnolia Loop with her casserole and a folding table, and Hal walks along grudgingly content, while Rosa, warm and hopeful, waits to host the dinner. Gary has already made his way to Rosa's place, and the whole group is gathering for supper as the golden light fades over Sumter Oaks.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Bench-test the light strings and speaker, refine the wiring sketch for Hal

gary.thought_process: I'm home at my workbench with the wiring and speaker sketch I drew up last tick. The Architectural Review application is already filed, and Hal said he'd sign off on my sketches himself. The cart stays in the garage and untouched until approval, so no one can write me up under L-01. Nobody is nearby to talk to, so the useful thing is to keep my hands busy and prepare. I'll go over the sketch and bench-test the light and speaker components on the workbench, which doesn't modify the cart's exterior, and clean up the layout so it's ready to hand to Hal and the board.

parameters.content: Bench-test the light strings and speaker, refine the wiring sketch for Hal

donna.thought_process: Hal and Rosa are both on the Loop, and dinner at Rosa's is waiting. Hal already agreed to look over my cart plans tomorrow, so no need to ask again. What I can do is keep the evening warm and nudge everyone toward the table, since Rosa's plate and my casserole are getting cold. I'll bring up the pickleball ladder with Gary at dinner, but right now the neighborly move is to get Hal moving and be glad about the parade committee.

parameters.content: Rosa, you're a doll for holding dinner. Hal, grab that folding table and let's go before my casserole turns into a doorstop. I'll walk over with you both.

hal.thought_process: Rosa told me to leave the notebook on the porch and come eat, and Donna just asked me to look over her cart plans tomorrow. Both have been answered or are waiting on me. I've already said my piece about rules and offered the folding table. Asking again would be repeating myself. The sensible move is to answer Donna's request plainly, accept the plate, and let the flamingo count stand at three. The notebook can wait until tomorrow. Order is fine, but a hot casserole is better.

parameters.content: Taking Rosa up on that plate. Notebook stays home. Donna's cart plans can come by tomorrow and I'll look them over then.

rosa.thought_process: Hal just asked what time dinner is and offered the folding table. I haven't answered him yet. Gary's already at my house, Donna is right here, and the casserole is getting cold. The point is to get all three neighbors at one table, so I give Hal a simple answer: dinner is on right now, and the table and chairs are welcome. Then I'll walk everyone over together.

parameters.content: Hal, dinner's right now. Gary's already at my place and Donna's casserole is waiting. Bring that folding table and the extra chairs and walk over with us, I'll save you a plate.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
